gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, the pick most of its answers named, gave only 231 Wh from its AC outlets in The Technology Man's test (about 80% of its 288 Wh rating). That is about the same as OutdoorGearLab's 230 Wh for the Anker SOLIX C300. OutdoorGearLab measured 620 Wh from the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro, and techtest.org measured an average of 272.9 Wh from the DC-only C300X DC.
standout_why: I opened PowerSized's kit price guide (powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/). It says it has not tested the units and uses an 85% usable-capacity planning assumption. Its only measured figure is OutdoorGearLab's panel result of 56–91% of rated watts. OffGridEmpire's under-$500 page has no test results, only advertised specs and its own $/Wh maths. StormWatts' same-panel-watts page has one owner test, on a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus with 800 W of panels, which is not an under-$500 kit. SolarGenAdvisor's under-$500 page (a cited rival) would not open because of a certificate error, so I could not check it. None of the pages I opened gives a named reviewer's measured usable Wh for any under-$500 candidate, or the Elite 30 V2's idle drain.
decides: This confirms the Elite 30 V2 as a 600 W-inverter pick, but its measured AC energy (231 Wh) is no better than the Anker C300's (230 Wh), so its edge is inverter size, not runtime. On the DC-only C300X DC, techtest.org measured 272.9 Wh from DC outputs. That is the most energy measured among the 288 Wh units, which fits USB and 12 V buyers. Where a RIVER 2 Pro kit is under $500, OutdoorGearLab's 620 Wh is about 2.7× the Elite 30 V2's measured AC output, which would make it the runtime pick. I did not check that kit's price (ChatGPT showed $429 at Sam's Club). The Elite 30 V2's idle drain with AC on and Eco mode off (100% to 19% in 12 h) also counts against it for overnight standby unless Eco mode is used.

unsourced: Jackery Explorer 300 v2 measured usable Wh. OutdoorGearLab's 260 Wh / 89% figure is for the original Explorer 300 (293 Wh claimed), not the v2. I found no named test of the v2, and searches turned up no techtest.org review of it.

EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus measured usable Wh. StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-02-12) reports '0.43 kWh' discharged from a 286 Wh unit, about 150% of its rating, so I treated that figure as unreliable and left it out. StorageReview's only other measurement was a UPS transfer time of 9 ms.
Anker SOLIX 536 measured usable Wh. I found no named review with a measurement; results only covered the 535 and listings.
ALLPOWERS P1800 measured usable Wh. I found no named review of this exact model. A BatterySkills result for an 'IEETek P1800' is a different brand, so I left it out.

BLUETTI EB3A measured usable Wh. Notebookcheck's hands-on test (Christian Hintze, 2023-01-10) measured about 102 W of solar input, but from the PV200 panel, not the 100 W panel in the kit, and it gives no measured usable Wh.
Measured solar charge time for any of these kits with its bundled panel (100 W BLUETTI, 40 W SolarSaga Air, 60 W Anker). I found no named reviewer test.
